issues.legal_issue: A court may treat a counterclaim included in a written statement as a plaint in a cross-suit when the pleading in substance states a claim and contains the necessary particulars for the relief sought.
material_facts: The defendants included a claim for accounts of a dissolved partnership in their written statement and described it as a counterclaim.
They valued the claim and paid the court fee applicable to a plaint seeking that relief.
The counterclaim was held not maintainable as a counterclaim, and the defendants asked that it be treated as a plaint in a cross-suit.
issues.conclusion: There was no legal objection to treating the counterclaim as a plaint in a cross-suit, and the High Court's order to do so was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: A counterclaim is statutory, and the claim here was not within Order VIII, rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. But that does not prevent a court from construing pleadings reasonably: where what is in substance a plaint is made part of a written statement, the court may treat it as a plaint and grant relief available on that pleading. Saya Bya v. Maung Kyaw Shun was relied on in support of this approach; Currimbhoy and Co. Ltd. v. Creet and (Mian) Pir Bux v. Mohomed Tahar establish that an unsupported counterclaim is not maintainable, but do not preclude its treatment as a cross-suit. Gour Chandra Goswami v. Chairman of the Nabadwip Municipality was distinguished.

rule.if: counterclaim_conversion_request and pleading_contains_independent_claim and pleading_supports_claimed_relief and cross_claim_properly_valued_and_fee_paid

predicates.counterclaim_conversion_request: A defendant asked the court to treat a claim included in a written statement as a plaint in a cross-suit.
predicates.pleading_contains_independent_claim: The written statement included a claim for relief independent of the plaintiff's claim.
predicates.pleading_supports_claimed_relief: The allegations in the written statement set out a claim capable of supporting the relief sought.
predicates.cross_claim_properly_valued_and_fee_paid: The defendant valued the cross-claim and paid the court fee applicable to the relief sought.

issues.definition: When a defendant asks to convert an independent claim in a written statement, and the pleading supports the relief and has been valued and stamped as required, the court may treat it as a plaint in a cross-suit.

issues.legal_issue: A defendant cannot obtain an accounting of a partnership merely from a plaintiff's pleadings when the plaintiff's suit seeks enforcement of an agreement rather than rendition of accounts.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought relief on the basis of an alleged agreement concerning dissolution of the partnership and settlement of the deceased partner's share.
The plaintiff's suit did not seek rendition of partnership accounts.
The defendants sought an accounting after the plaintiff failed to prove the alleged agreement.
issues.conclusion: The defendants were not entitled to an accounting on the pleadings of the plaintiff's suit; their claim required a separate claim treated as a plaint in a cross-suit.
issues.legal_principle: Authorities treating a defendant in a suit for accounts as virtually a plaintiff apply where accounting relief is common to the parties. They do not apply where the plaintiff seeks enforcement of an agreement and does not ask for accounts. The Court distinguished decisions concerning section 69(3)(a) of the Partnership Act, 1932.

predicates.plaintiff_suit_seeks_agreement_enforceme: The plaintiff brought the suit to enforce an alleged agreement concerning the parties' rights.
predicates.plaintiff_suit_seeks_partnership_account: The plaintiff's suit sought rendition of partnership accounts.
predicates.defendant_seeks_partnership_accounts: The defendant sought an accounting of the partnership.

issues.definition: If a suit seeks enforcement of an agreement rather than partnership accounts, a defendant seeking accounts cannot obtain that relief from the plaintiff's pleadings alone.

issues.legal_issue: For limitation purposes, a cross-suit formed by treating a counterclaim as a plaint is treated as filed when the written statement containing the counterclaim was filed, if conversion adds no allegations or relief.
material_facts: The defendants' written statement contained the claim for partnership accounts and was filed within the applicable limitation period.
The defendants later requested that the counterclaim be treated as a plaint in a cross-suit.
They sought no new allegations or relief in the conversion, and the claim had already been valued and stamped as a plaint.
issues.conclusion: The cross-suit was treated as filed on the date the written statement containing the counterclaim was filed, not on the date the court ordered conversion.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, leave to amend will ordinarily be refused where an amendment takes away a legal right accrued by lapse of time, save in exceptional cases. That principle applies to added allegations or fresh relief, not a clarification that does not substantively add to or alter the original pleading. The Court approved the rule in the Bombay High Court decision in Bai Bhuri v. Rai Ambalal Chotalal. It also referred to Article 106 of the Limitation Act when considering the limitation period for the accounting claim.

predicates.counterclaim_conversion_request: A defendant asked the court to treat a claim included in a written statement as a plaint in a cross-suit.
predicates.original_pleading_contains_claim: The written statement already contained the claim later treated as a cross-suit.
predicates.conversion_adds_no_allegations_or_relief: Treating the claim as a plaint does not add allegations or seek relief not contained in the original pleading.

issues.definition: If a written statement already contains the claim and its conversion adds no allegations or relief, the cross-suit is treated as filed when that written statement was filed.

issues.legal_issue: Partnership accounting issues concerning a surviving partner's use of firm assets and the firm's goodwill do not, by themselves, prevent a counterclaim from being treated as a plaint in a cross-suit.
material_facts: The defendants sought accounts following dissolution of the partnership.
The trial court relied on section 37 of the Partnership Act, 1932 and the potential need to determine the existence and value of goodwill when refusing conversion.
The counterclaim had been presented as a claim for accounts, and the conversion did not itself determine the substantive accounting issues.
issues.conclusion: Neither the possible application of section 37 nor the existence or valuation of goodwill was a legally sufficient reason to refuse conversion.
issues.legal_principle: Section 37 of the Partnership Act, 1932 states the substantive liability of a surviving or continuing partner who uses partnership assets to continue the business without final settlement of accounts; it does not bar conversion of a claim for accounts. Under section 55(1), goodwill is included among the firm's assets when accounts are settled after dissolution, subject to any agreement between the partners, and may be sold separately or with other property.

predicates.counterclaim_conversion_request: A defendant asked the court to treat a claim included in a written statement as a plaint in a cross-suit.
predicates.cross_suit_seeks_dissolved_partnership_a: The proposed cross-suit seeks accounts of a dissolved partnership.
predicates.objection_concerns_continuing_partner_li: The objection to conversion concerns liability arising from use of firm assets after a partner's departure or the treatment of goodwill in settling accounts.

issues.definition: When a proposed cross-suit seeks accounts of a dissolved partnership, objections based on continuing-partner liability or goodwill do not by themselves prevent conversion.

issues.legal_issue: When a counterclaim is treated as a plaint in a cross-suit, both sides may be allowed to file fresh pleadings that conform to their new procedural roles, provided the claim is not substantially changed.
material_facts: The plaintiff's reply had been filed in response to a counterclaim rather than a plaint in a cross-suit.
The defendants sought permission to replace the counterclaim with a pleading in the form of a plaint.
The defendants' replacement pleading was to contain no substantial variation in allegations or relief.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was allowed to file a fresh written statement, and the defendants were allowed to file a fresh plaint provided there was no substantial variation in their allegations or relief.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that fairness required the plaintiff to have an opportunity to plead defences to the claim as a cross-suit. It permitted the defendants to recast their pleading in the form of a plaint subject to the stated restriction, without limiting the court's power to permit later amendment under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

predicates.counterclaim_treated_as_cross_suit: The court treated a claim included in a written statement as a plaint in a cross-suit.
predicates.existing_reply_filed_to_counterclaim: The plaintiff's existing response was filed on the footing that the claim was a counterclaim.
predicates.replacement_claim_substantially_unchange: The replacement pleading makes no substantial variation in the allegations or relief sought.

issues.definition: When a counterclaim becomes a cross-suit, the parties may file pleadings suited to their new roles if the replacement claim is substantially unchanged.
